title: LLMs for Mathematical Modeling: Towards Bridging the Gap between Natural and Mathematical Languages

model.params_source: paper Appendix Q ('We tested the following models by calling API: All the closed source models except o1-preview ... with temperature=0.8'); max_length 4096 is stated for the locally served models and is taken over here

task.subset_rule: all of Mamo: 346 ODE + 652 Easy_LP + 211 Complex_LP problems (Sec. 3.5)
task.approximation: blocked: the few-shot examples are elided in the printed prompts and scoring executes the generated code (see open_points). The claim is the raw score, i.e. before the code-modifier repair pass, so only the first generation of each problem is needed.

items.source: github.com/FreedomIntelligence/Mamo (Mamo: a Mathematical Modeling Benchmark with Solvers)

download.check: HEAD 200, 245,048 bytes for data/ode/mamo_ode.jsonl; the two optimization files are listed under data/optimization/Easy_LP/ and data/optimization/Complex_LP/ in the repository tree. Row schema from the README: {id, Question, Answer, Category: ode|optimization, Type: first_order_equation|...|easy_lp|complex_lp}. Files were not downloaded (the cell is blocked for other reasons).

prompt.few_shot: k=3 fixed examples ('We use 3-shot in testing', caption of Figure 17), but only Example_1 of the optimization prompt is printed; the remaining examples are replaced by '[...]' in both figures
prompt.source_location: Appendix R (Figures 17 and 18; Figures 19-20 are the code-modifier prompts, which the raw score does not use)
prompt.verbatim: partial: the instruction blocks are printed in full and are transcribed above in condensed form, but the few-shot demonstrations are elided ('[...]' / '[Examples]'), so the exact prompt cannot be reconstructed from the paper.

output.postprocess: the reply is an .lp file (optimization) or a Python program (ODE); it is written to disk and executed, and the solver's / program's numeric output is compared with the ground truth

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Overall accuracy rate (%) over the 1,209 problems: the generated .lp file is solved with an LP solver (the repository uses COPT) and the generated Python is executed; a problem counts as correct when the produced value matches the ground truth, per the paper's own check 'abs(ans - s_ans) < 1 or comp(output, standard_answer)' (Appendix P). 'Raw' means before the code-modifier repair pass whose gain the table shows as a subscript (+1.41).
metric.original_location: Table 4, row GPT-4-turbo, Overall(%) column: 66.34 with subscript +1.41 for the code-modifier variant

cost.prepare_note: not run: prompt incomplete. 1,209 problems at gpt-4-turbo $10/$30 per 1M with long 3-shot prompts and code answers is roughly $50 per seed.

open_points: prompt: 3-shot is used, but the demonstrations are printed as '[...]' / '[Examples]'. Writing our own three examples would change the prompt, and for a code-generation task the examples are a large part of it. The repository would have to be read for the actual few-shot block - a human decision about how far to go outside the paper.

scoring: the metric requires executing the model's output - solving generated .lp files with an LP/MILP solver (COPT in the repository; a swap to another solver is a decision) and running generated Python with SciPy/SymPy. That is sandboxed code execution, which this harness does not do.

seeds: the paper ran at temperature 0.8, so the cell is stochastic. The schema gives the high cost tier one seed, which cannot show that run-to-run spread; a decision is needed on whether the raw score is worth extra passes.
notes: Data and licence are in order (CC BY-SA 4.0, files reachable on GitHub); the blockers are the elided few-shot examples and the execution-based scoring. Table 6 adds an o1-preview / GPT-4-0613 code-modifier variant, and Table 4's subscripts are the same repair pass; the claim here is the raw column.
